subject: Delta Health — Transfer framework & DPF implementation questions
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@deltahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>; Delta Health Procurement <procurement@deltahealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Delta Health — data transfer framework & DPF implementation questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our vendor review for the Delta Health inference pilot, our legal and privacy teams asked us to collect a few specific artifacts and clarifications on cross-border transfers and the Data Protection Framework (DPF) posture. Could you provide the following by COB Monday (2026-11-30)?

1) A data flow mapping that shows where patient-generated and system-derived data transits (including any third-party subprocessors and cloud regions).
2) Draft DPA Annex that covers cross-border transfers and the safeguards you propose (SCCs, EU-US DPF, other contractual measures).
3) Confirmation of encryption in transit and at rest (algorithms and KMS integration).
4) Operational logs / sample audit entries showing data access and deletions (redacted).
5) Clarify whether Redwood will act as processor only, and confirm the subprocessors list and subprocessor onboarding/notification process.
6) Any limitations on residency (can we keep PHI in EU-only for initial pilot) and whether you support regional routing / private deployment.

If you have a standard packet for privacy evidence, feel free to send that. If you need to triage items, let us know what you can provide first.

Appreciate it — we want to keep timeline tight so our security review can proceed.

Emily
Emily Chen
Senior Procurement Manager, Delta Health Systems

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. High-level plan below and I'll follow up with attachments by end of day Tuesday (2026-11-30):

- We will provide a mapping PDF that highlights: ingress points, regional routing, subprocessors, and retention points. (attachment: redwood_dpf-mapping.pdf)
- Draft DPA Annex for your review with proposed contractual safeguards (attachment: dpa-annex-deltahealth-v1.docx). Our standard approach is SCCs + contractual annex; where DPF is requested we can provide implementation notes but final acceptance typically requires customer legal signoff.
- Encryption: TLS1.2+ for transit, AES-256 at rest; KMS integrations supported (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). We'll include a short tech note.
- Logs: redacted sample operational logs (attachment: operational-logs-sample.txt).
- Subprocessors: full list + notification process included in annex.

Quick clarifying question: when you say "PHI in EU-only for initial pilot" — is that a strict requirement (no US-hosted processing at all), or a strong preference? That will determine whether we recommend a private deployment path or a hosted configuration with EU-region routing and contractual constraints.

Cc'ing Karthik (legal) and Marissa (ops) to confirm timelines and sign off on the annex and mapping.

If helpful we can lock a 30-minute call Wednesday to walk through the mapping and the DPA draft.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head, Security & Privacy — Redwood Inference

Soojin / Marissa — quick notes from Legal after an initial review: 

1) DPA Annex: our standard annex + SCCs is acceptable. We should not pre-agree to the EU-US DPF as a blanket contractual commitment; we can provide implementation-level notes on how we operationalize transfers under DPF when requested by the customer. If Delta requires DPF attestation, route to Sales & Legal for a scoped evaluation.

2) Deletion / retention obligations: we can commit to documented retention schedules and deletion workflows, but avoid unlimited liabilities for past-data reconstruction. If Delta tries to require immediate purging across all caches within unrealistic windows, propose a defined SLA (e.g., deletion initiated within 72 hours, complete in xx days depending on cache replication).

3) Subprocessors: provide current list and commit to 30 days' notification for additions. No objection to a review period; non-material subprocessors can be handled via standard notice.

If Delta insists on EU-only physical processing for PHI we should evaluate Private deployment options (customer-managed VPC or on-prem) — that is feasible but requires procurement lead time and potentially a different commercial profile.

I'll review the annex doc and mark redlines by EOD Monday.

— Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FW: Delta Health — data transfer framework & DPF implementation questions

Attaching the requested mapping and log sample. Highlights:

- Data map: primary ingestion in EU (eu-west-1) is supported for hosted customers in that region; our standard hosted pipeline routes inference requests to the nearest region unless pinned. For customers requiring EU-only residency for both at-rest and processing, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) which pins all compute and storage to the customer's chosen region. See notes in the mapping (attachment: redwood_dpf-mapping.pdf).

- Subprocessors: list included in annex; major ones are Cloud Provider (AWS), observability vendor (Datadog), and managed backup vendor (BackupCo). We redact internal IDs in the log sample. (attachment: operational-logs-sample.txt).

- Operational nuance: we maintain short-lived caches (KV caches) for inference efficiency; deletion flows will invalidate caches but full removal from distributed backups can take up to 14 days depending on replication windows — propose a contractual SLA instead of immediate destruction demand.

Files attached: redwood_dpf-mapping.pdf, operational-logs-sample.txt

Let me know if you want a short diagram I can add for the call.

— Marissa

Subject: Re: Delta Health — Transfer framework & DPF implementation questions (attachments and next steps)

Hi Emily — apologies for the slight push on timing and thank you for your patience. Attached are the documents we discussed and a short summary of the answers below. If anything needs refinement we can iterate quickly or jump on a short call.

Attachments included:
- redwood_dpf-mapping.pdf (dataflow, subprocessors, recommended routing)
- dpa-annex-deltahealth-v1.docx (draft annex with SCCs and standard language)
- operational-logs-sample.txt (redacted access/audit entries)

Summary answers (short):
1) Data flow mapping: Ingest can be pinned to EU regions. Hosted customers in eu-west-1 will have compute and storage in EU; by default hosted routing is region-aware but not residency-enforced. Private deployment pins processing and storage to selected region (recommended for strict EU-only PHI). See mapping doc for subprocessors and handoff points.

2) DPA Annex & safeguards: Draft annex attached. Our standard position is SCCs + contractual annex. We can provide DPF implementation notes but cannot unilaterally attest to DPF on behalf of Redwood without a scoped legal review; if Delta requires DPF attestation we will coordinate between Legal and Sales to confirm feasibility.

3) Encryption: TLS1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. We support AWS KMS and GCP KMS integration and will include key rotation and access control notes in the annex.

4) Operational logs: redacted samples attached. Logs include request IDs, model_id, timestamp, operator/service account ID. Full audit exports can be provided under NDA if required.

5) Subprocessors: full list in annex; we commit to 30 days' notification for additions.

6) EU-only residency request: Feasible via Private deployment or a hosted EU-only configuration with contractual commitments. Private deployment is the stronger guarantee and avoids cross-border subprocessors, but requires procurement and lead time (estimate: 6–8 weeks for initial provisioning + onboarding).

Proposed next steps: 
- If Delta wants to proceed with the hosted EU routing option, confirm region and we will provide an implementation plan and org-level contact for onboarding.
- If Delta requires Private (EU-only) deployment, let's schedule a technical scoping call (30 minutes) next week to align on timelines and commercial terms.

Suggested times for a short call: Wed 12/2 09:00–11:30 PT or Thu 12/3 14:00–16:00 PT. Share a preferred slot and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks again — happy to answer follow-ups.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Head, Security & Privacy — Redwood Inference
